subject: air-combat
title: Basic Fighter Maneuvers
objective: Understand one-versus-one BFM geometry, pursuit, turn performance, vertical maneuvering, energy and guns employment well enough to describe what each aircraft is doing and why.
applicability: Aircraft-agnostic concepts illustrated with US Navy T-45C training figures; type-specific numbers belong to that training example.

subject: airfield-operations
title: The Airfield and the Traffic Pattern
objective: Read a military airfield's runway numbers, markings, arresting gear, signs and lighting, read the PAPI and the Navy optical landing system, choose the runway in use from the wind, fly the overhead and the standard pattern, know where helicopters fly, make military field calls, and move safely on the ground.
applicability: Military pilots of all US services first: Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and Army airfield practice, with shared US (FAA) standards and civil towered and non-towered procedures as supplementary. Each military field's course rules and published procedures take precedence.

subject: radio-communications
title: Radio Procedures and Phraseology
objective: Speak and understand military air–ground radio: multi-service brevity words, a training sortie's calls, call signs and preset channels, formation check-ins and training-rule calls, then the FAA technique, phonetic alphabet and numbers, contact calls, readbacks, emergency calls, transponder codes and what to do when the radio fails.
applicability: For US military pilots of all services: the joint Army, Marine Corps, Navy and Air Force brevity codes and a worked Navy training sortie first, with the FAA Aeronautical Information Manual as the supplementary US civil rule set; units and other countries differ in detail.

subject: flight-fundamentals
title: Principles of Flight
objective: Understand the four forces, lift and angle of attack, drag, control and stability, turns and load factor, stalls, the maneuvering envelope, energy and rotor-wing aerodynamics well enough to explain what a military jet or helicopter is doing and why.
applicability: For military pilots of every service: fixed- and rotary-wing principles from Navy aerodynamics texts and the Army's Fundamentals of Flight, with FAA handbooks as supplementary sources; worked numbers use an invented jet trainer and rotor, with US Navy T-45 training figures where cited.

subject: navigation
title: Air Navigation
objective: Read the HSI as a picture, set up and fly a TACAN or VOR course, correct for wind, intercept courses inbound and outbound, fly DME arcs, point to point and waypoint routes, and cross-check them, with positions, headings and the navigation aids as background.
applicability: For military pilots of every service: US Navy training publications first, with the FAA AIM and Pilot's Handbook as the supplementary US civil rule set and an Army field manual for the military grid. Worked examples use the T-45C training jet's displays; your aircraft's flight manual (NATOPS or your service's equivalent) governs its systems.
